summary: Discord.js impersonator smuggles mandatory dependency from private GitHub repo via embedded PAT
details: @velliajs/discord@1.0.3 presents itself as a discord.js library (name '@velliajs/discord', description 'Discord Bot Libray By Valera', repository field pointing at discordjs/discord.js, main re-exports the discord.js API surface) but declares a mandatory `sysframe` dependency resolved from `git+https://ghp_<redacted>@github.com/navaLinh/node-ai.git`. npm resolves this git+https URL during `npm install`, using the embedded GitHub personal access token to pull code from a private repository controlled by the author. The fetched module is added to the installer's dependency graph and its own lifecycle scripts and require-time code execute on the installer's host. The private-repo delivery channel places the code outside npm registry inspection, and the fetched contents can be changed by the author at any time without republishing this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
